Gingrich Says Teen Smoking Not Caused by Joe Camel.
Medical Marijuana, Needle Exchange "Send Wrong Message"

The Clinton administration declared yesterday that needle exchange programs can help curb the AIDS epidemic without fostering the use of illegal drugs, but refused to allow federal money to be spent on the programs.

Even saying that the needle exchange programs work "is an intolerable message that it's time to accept drug use as a way of life," said Sen. John D. Ashcroft (Mo.), one of several Republicans who denounced the administration's decision.

Today House Speaker Newt Gingrich attacked proposed bipartisan anti-smoking legislation, saying teen smoking had no connection with the well-known Joe Camel advertising campaign. In order to understand what's happened with teen smoking, this is not complicated. It has nothing to do with Joe Camel."

Gingrich said that a much greater cause of teen smoking was the example of Hollywood stars smoking on screen and he cited the example of "Titanic" and its male lead Leonardo DiCaprio. He also assailed Clinton for smoking cigars --  but not yet for serving alcohol at the White House.

Both Gingrich and Clinton think that the Federal government should be actively involved in the suppression of medical marijuana because it would "send the wrong message to teenagers."

The federal government is massively involved in health care, especially in dealing with AIDS, but it cannot fund the program that would do much to reduce its incidence. Meanwhile, it can use nine marshals and four prosecutors to try to lock up Todd McCormick, just one medical marijuana user.

Gingrich says that a multimillion dollar ad campaign featuring a cartoon character does not sell young people cigarettes, but allowing sick people to have medical cannabis would sell them marijuana.

In addition, the Republicans killed a proposal that would have mandated a national standard for drunk driving, because it would interfere with states’ rights, while they are supporting a resolution says that the states should not allow medical marijuana while the Federal government opposes it.

Given the name and focus of this web site it is natural for me to view issues from the "marijuana perspective," but I maintain that it is intellectually and morally necessary to object to this hypocrisy and absurdity. When the purpose and very real consequence is massive human suffering, this anti-sense is about much more than marijuana. This is about maintaining the very meaning of life.
